title: PRMT5: a Novel Regulator of Hepatitis B Virus Replication and an Arginine Methylase of HBV Core

steps_raw.instruction: Quantification of HBV cccDNA
(adapted from Xia Y, Stadler D, Ko C, Protzer U. Analyses of HBV cccDNA Quantification
and Modification. Methods Mol Biol. 2017;1540:59-72).
1. Isolate total intracellular DNA from HBV-infected HepG2_hNTCP cells using Qiamp DNA Blood MiniKit (Qiagen).

2. Treat the total intracellular DNA with T5 exonuclease (NEB). Mix 8.5 l of DNA with 1 l of 10x NEB buffer 4 and 0.5 l of T5 exonuclease. Mix and incubate at 37 oC for 30 min followed by heat inactivation at 100 oC for 5 min. Dilute each sample with 30 l of distilled water. Proceed to qPCR:

3. The levels of cccDNA were analyzed by qPCR using an Eppendorf realplex Master cycler and gb Elite PCR Master Mix (Generi Biotech). Mix 5 µl of T5 exonuclease-treated DNA, 0.6 l of cccDNA-F primer 5′- CCGTGTGCACTTCGCTTCA -3′ (10 M), 0.6 l of cccDNA-R primer 5′- GCACAGCTTGGAGGCTTGA -3′ (10 M), 0.4 l of cccDNA probe 5′-[FAM]CATGGAGACCACCGTGAACGCCC[BHQ1]-3′ (5 M), 10 l of 2x gb Elite Master Mix and 3.4 l of PCR grade water.

The recommended thermal cycling conditions for qPCR run are: denaturation (95°C for 10 min), denaturation and annealing/elongation steps repeated 40 times with fluorescence measurement at the end of the elongation step (95°C for 15 s, 60°C for 1 min).

4. Normalize the levels of cccDNA to the levels of albumin determined by qPCR using primers: Alb-F 5'-GCTGTCATCTCTTGTGGGCTGT-3'; Alb-R 5'-AAACTCATGGGAGCTGCTGGTT-3'; and Alb-probe 5'-[FAM]GGAGAGATTTGTGTGGGCATGACAGG[BHQ1]-3'. The conditions for qPCR are the same as for cccDNA amplification.
Co-immnunoprecipitation of HA-tagged proteins expressed in human cells
(For the best results, determine optimal conditions for expression of HA-tagged fusion protein before attempting immunoprecipitation.)
Wash transfected cells with pre-chilled 1xPBS.
Add in cold co-immunoprecipitation buffer (20 mM HEPES [pH 7.9], 50 mM NaCl, 5 mM EDTA, 1% (v/v) Igepal CA-630, 10% (v/v) glycerol, 1 mM dithiothreitol).
To minimize protein degradation, add the protease inhibitors to the lysis buffer prior to use (1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF), and 0.2 mM protease inhibitor cocktail [all Sigma-Aldrich]).
Scrap cells and transfer into 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes.
Incubate on ice with frequent mixing for 20 min.
Centrifuge at 14,000 g, 4 °C, for 20 min and transfer the supernatant to fresh tubes.
Estimate the protein concentration using Coomassie (Bradford) Protein Assay Kit (Pierce).
Prepare anti-HA Magnetic beads (Pierce) for immunoprecipitation:
For each analyzed sample pipet 25 l of magnetic beads into a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Wash beads with 1 ml of 1x PBS, gently vortex to mix.
Place the tube into magnetic stand and remove the supernatant.
Repeat he whole procedure three times.

8. Add the sample containing HA-tagged protein (400 g of total protein diluted in 600 l of lysis buffer) to the pre-washed magnetic beads and incubate at 4 °C for 4 h to overnight with constant mixing.
9. Collect the beads with a magnetic stand, remove the unbound sample and save for analysis.
10. Wash beads five times with 1 ml of lysis buffer.
11. After the last wash, denature the bound proteins in 2x sample loading buffer by boiling at 100 °C for 5 min.
12. Analyze the precipitated proteins by SDS-PAGE and Western blot.
Detection of ubiquitinated proteins in cells

1. Transfect cells with expression plasmid for studied protein tagged with HA or Flag tags using Lipofectamine 2000 or 3000 (ThermoFisher) or other type of transfection reagent. (For transfection procedure, follow the manufacturer’s instructions).
2. Two days post-transfection, wash cells with ice-cold 1xPBS.

3. Scrape the cells into lysis buffer (2% SDS, 150 mM NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, supplemented with 2mM sodium orthovanadate, 50 mM sodium fluoride, 10 mM N-ethylmaleimide (NEM) and protease inhibitors) into 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube. Use approximately 500 l lysis buffer per one T75 flask.
4. Denature the samples by boiling at 100oC for 10 min.
5. Shear the cells by sonication.
6. Dilute the lysates with 9 volumes of dilution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 2 mM EDTA, 1% Triton).
7. Centrifuge the cell lysates at maximum speed for 20 min in table-top Eppendorf centrifuge and transfer the supernatant into a fresh tube.
8. Estimate the protein concentration using Coomassie (Bradford) Protein Assay Kit (Pierce).
9. Prepare anti-HA (Pierce) or anti-Flag (Sigma) magnetic beads for immunoprecipitations:
For each analyzed sample use 25 l of magnetic beads.
Wash beads with 1 ml of 1x PBS, gently vortex to mix.
Place the tube into magnetic stand and remove the supernatant.
Repeat he whole procedure three times.
10. Pipet 25 l of washed magnetic beads into 500 g of cell lysate. If the expression of studied protein is very low, up to 1500 g of protein lysate may be needed.
11. Incubate the protein lysate-bead mixture with constant rotating at 4oC overnight.
12. Collect the beads using a magnetic stand, remove the unbound sample and save for analysis.
10. Wash beads three times with 1 ml of wash buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 1 M NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1% NP-40).
11. After the last wash, denature the bound proteins in 2x sample loading buffer by boiling at 100 °C for 5 min.
12. Analyze the precipitated proteins by SDS-PAGE and Western blot with anti-Ubiquitin antibodies (Cell Signaling).
Mass spectrometry analysis (LC-MS/MS)

The SDS-PAGE the coumasie stained gel was devided into 14 pieces. Gel pieces were destained with ammonium bicarbonate in 50 % acetonitrile at 30°C for 30 min and dried with 200 μl acetonitrile for 5 min at 30°C. Dry gel pieces were treated with dithiothreitol (65°C, 30 min) and Iodoacetamide (RT for 30 min in dark) to reduce and alkylate cysteins. Proteins in gel pieces were digested with 0.1 μg of trypsin solution in ammonium bicarbonate at 37°C for 10 hours. Peptides were extracted with 50 μl of 2 % TFA and 50 μl of 60 % acetonitrile. The peptides were dried in the SpeedVac and dissolved in 15 µl of 0.1 % formic acid.
2. On-beads digestion

Immunoprecipitated proteins on magnetic beads were washed 3x with 1ml of 50 mM ammonium hydrocarbonate. Proteins in the sample were reduced by dithiothreitol (65°C, 30 min) and alkylated by Iodoacetamide (RT for 30 min in dark). Solvent was removed, 100ul of 50 mM ammonium hydrocarbonate including 0,1 μg of chymotrypsin were added and proteins were digested at 37°C for 10 hours. Resulting peptides were separated from beads by magnet, dried in the SpeedVac (Labconco) and dissolved in 15 µl of 0.1 % formic acid.

All samples were analyzed on UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system (Dionex – Thermo Scientific) coupled to a TripleTOF 5600 mass spectrometer with a NanoSpray III source (Sciex). The instrument was operated with Analyst TF 1.7 (Sciex). The peptides were trapped and desalted with 2 % acetonitrile in 0.1 % formic acid at flow rate of 5 μL/min on Acclaim PepMap100 column (5 μm, 2 cm×100 μm ID, Thermo Scientific). Eluted peptides were separated using Acclaim PepMap100 analytical column (3 μm, 25 cm×75 μm ID, Thermo Scientific). The 70 min elution gradient at constant flow of 300 nl/min was set to 5 % of phase B (0.1 % formic acid in 99.9 % acetonitrile, phase A 0.1 % formic acid) for first 5 min, then with gradient elution by increasing content of acetonitrile. TOF MS mass range was set to 350–1500 m/z, in MS/MS mode the instrument acquired fragmentation spectra within m/z range 100-2000.
